core_meaning.primary_meaning: Jandab (جُنْدَب) is an authentic Arabic masculine given name meaning 'agile, energetic mover' or 'resilient desert champion'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned personal name of the heroic early companion Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (Jandab ibn Junadah), celebrated for uncompromised truthfulness, as well as Jandab ibn Abdillah al-Bajali.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: A classical Arabic name representing energetic alertness, swift motion, and unyielding self-reliance in the open desert.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Jandab ibn Junadah al-Ghifari was the fourth or fifth person to accept Islam in Mecca. He walked alone into Mecca to seek the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and boldly proclaimed the Shahada before Quraysh at the Kaaba. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gave him the immortal tribute recorded in Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 'There is no one under the sky or above the earth more truthful in speech than Abu Dharr.'

faq.a: Jandab (جُنْدَب) is an authentic Arabic masculine given name meaning 'agile, energetic mover' or 'resilient desert champion'. faq.q: What is the origin of Jandab?
faq.a: Jandab ibn Junadah al-Ghifari was the fourth or fifth person to accept Islam in Mecca. He walked alone into Mecca to seek the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and boldly proclaimed the Shahada before Quraysh at the Kaaba. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gave him the immortal tribute recorded in Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 'There is no one under the sky or above the earth more truthful in speech than Abu Dharr.'
Yes. The recorded language/origin is Arabic; the source form is جُنْدَب.

faq.q: How is Jandab written in Arabic?

faq.a: It is not claimed as a Qur'anic personal name. Jandab is not in the Qur'an; its Islamic stature is established by authentic prophetic hadiths honoring Abu Dharr.
